title: Evidence-only performance trace for one run
description: A schema-validated DERIVED view over a stored run's recorded timing/identity fields, assembled by clozn.runs.perf_trace.build_trace() -- not a second copy persisted alongside the run. clock: 'monotonic' is a contract on `phases`: every phases[].duration_ns in this document is sourced from a monotonic clock (Python time.monotonic_ns() or the C++ worker's std::chrono::steady_clock), never from a wall-clock delta, so NTP adjustment or a system clock step cannot produce a negative or skewed phase duration. Wall-clock-derived totals (e.g. the gateway's started_at/ended_at timestamps) are correlation-only and live under `metrics.wall_clock_total_ms`, explicitly named so a reader never mistakes them for a phases[] entry with monotonic provenance. A key or array entry this run's evidence cannot support is OMITTED, never null-padded or estimated -- absence must stay visible.

clock.description: The clock family every phases[].duration_ns in this document is sourced from. 'monotonic' is the only value v1 emits.

machine_identity.description: The run's identity.ext.machine facet (clozn/runs/identity_providers/machine.py), when the run recorded one. Absent entirely on runs captured before that provider shipped, or when every field it could report was itself unmeasurable -- never present-and-empty.

engine_identity.description: The subset of the run's top-level identity block (clozn/runs/identity.py) that identifies the engine/model/build that produced this trace: model_sha256, template_fingerprint, engine_build, clozn_version. A field absent here means the run's identity block never captured it, not that it was empty.

phases.description: Monotonic-clock phase spans. Only phases this run's evidence actually supports are present -- an unmeasured phase (queue, model_load, prefill, ... per the roadmap spec) is omitted from this array entirely rather than emitted with a zero or guessed duration.

name.description: Open vocabulary (not a closed enum): future features add phase names -- e.g. 'adapter_load' -- without a schema edit here. See docs/agent_roadmap/09-performance-diagnosis.md's 'Required phases' list for the intended names.

owner.description: Which side of the ownership boundary this phase's time is charged to, per the spec's 'Ownership boundaries' -- so a slow external tool or client backpressure is never presented as the model's fault.

clock_owner.description: Process that sampled this phase's monotonic clock. Offsets may only be compared within the same clock_domain.

clock_domain.description: Stable display label for the local monotonic domain, e.g. clozn_worker:steady_clock. It is not a globally synchronized clock.

measurement.description: Measured phases come from an instrumented clock. Estimated is reserved for explicitly modeled values and is never included in known_duration_ns.

aggregation.description: Only exclusive measured phases contribute to known_duration_ns. Overlapping spans are useful attribution but would double-count another phase; context_only phases occurred outside the run wall interval.

start_ns.description: Nanoseconds since this trace's first recorded span (relative, not an absolute clock reading). OPTIONAL: omitted when this phase's offset within the request isn't known, even though its own duration is -- e.g. a decode duration recorded with no queue/load timing recorded before it to anchor against.

metrics.description: Whole-request counters and rates. Open for extension (additionalProperties: true) since later slices add fields without a schema bump.

wall_clock_total_ms.description: The gateway's started_at/ended_at delta. Explicitly NOT a phases[] entry: it is wall-clock-derived (time.time(), not monotonic), so it is correlation-only and must never be summed with phases[].duration_ns as if the two shared a clock domain.

aggregation.description: Arithmetic over measured, exclusive phases only. Cross-process offsets are never subtracted.

events.description: Advanced, opt-in raw events (e.g. per-token timing) -- present only when advanced tracing was enabled for this run. v1's default derivation never populates this.

regression_attribution.description: Summary of evidence-gated rules that attributed a likely regression. This is never upgraded beyond the strongest evidence state carried by those rules.

diagnoses.description: One entry per rule clozn.runs.perf_diagnosis evaluated, whether or not it could fire -- a rule the evidence could not support is listed with status 'unavailable' and a stated reason, never silently omitted, so the absence of a warning is never mistaken for 'nothing wrong here'.

status.description: 'fired': the rule's evidence was present and its condition was met. 'not_fired': the rule's evidence was present and evaluated, but the condition was NOT met -- an explicit, present 'checked and clean' entry, never silence. 'unavailable': the evidence this rule needs does not exist on this run at all (usually because no code path records it yet) -- distinct from not_fired so a reader can never mistake 'we don't have this instrumented' for 'we checked and it's fine'.

reason.description: Required in practice when status is 'unavailable' or 'not_fired': names exactly what evidence was missing, or what was checked and found not to meet the rule's threshold.

evidence_state.description: Required in practice when status is 'fired': how strongly the evidence supports the cause, using the roadmap's explicit vocabulary. This artifact never emits 'causally_supported' without a real replay intervention behind it.
